edges.description: Intestinal ZIP4 loss rapidly depletes tissue zinc and causes wasting and death unless excess dietary zinc is supplied.
edges.limitations: The global Zip4 knockout is embryonic lethal, unlike human AE where residual function is retained, and the intestine-specific model is an acute, complete-loss model that does not reproduce the skin phenotype.

edges.description: The knockout reprograms Paneth cells and disrupts the intestinal stem cell niche and mucosal integrity.
edges.limitations: An acute, complete-loss intestinal model rather than the chronic partial-loss state of most human patients.

evidence.reference_title: A novel member of a zinc transporter family is defective in acrodermatitis enteropathica.
evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that the hZIP4 transporter is responsible for intestinal absorption of zinc.

nodes.description: Zinc is a catalytic or structural cofactor for hundreds of metalloenzymes and zinc-finger transcription factors. Its depletion impairs rapidly renewing epithelia (skin, hair follicle) and immune cells most acutely, producing the cutaneous and immune features of the disease.

evidence.snippet: Zinc is an essential and versatile element, utilized by proteins as diverse as metalloenzymes and transcription factors.

nodes.description: Zinc depletion reprograms Paneth cells and disrupts the intestinal stem cell niche, degrading the integrity of the absorptive epithelium; in the mouse model this drives the wasting phenotype and is the correlate of the diarrhea and malabsorption seen in patients.

nodes.description: Erythematous, scaly, vesiculobullous or psoriasiform dermatitis distributed acrally (hands, feet, limbs) and around the mouth, anus, and perineum.

evidence.reference_title: Acrodermatitis enteropathica in the pediatric population: a literature review of real-world studies.
evidence.snippet: the lesions were most commonly present on the hands and feet and limbs (187 patients, 83.1%), followed by the perioral area (171 patients, 76.0%) and the perianal area (163 patients, 72.4%).

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC39A4, which encodes the apical zinc transporter ZIP4 of the enterocyte, abolish or reduce its zinc transport activity.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of SLC39A4, a gene involved in acrodermatitis enteropathica.
evidence.snippet: mutational analysis of eight families affected with acrodermatitis enteropathica, suggest that SLC39A4 is centrally involved in the pathogenesis of this condition

evidence.snippet: The rare inherited condition acrodermatitis enteropathica (AE) results from a defect in the absorption of dietary zinc.

nodes.description: Failure of intestinal zinc absorption depletes systemic zinc, lowering plasma zinc and the activity of zinc-dependent enzymes and transcription factors throughout the body.
